behaviors.stress_management: When stressed, he may eat something convenient, stay up scrolling or watching television, or go quiet for a while. He sometimes talks things through with Elena, his mother, or a trusted sibling. He knows a walk helps his mood but does not always choose it when tired.
behaviors.sleep: Often stays up late for personal quiet time, entertainment, or phone use after his daughter is asleep. He sometimes gets less sleep than he needs and then relies on coffee or a steady routine to get through the morning.

health.overall: No major diagnosed condition is specified. He is capable of physical outdoor work and ordinary daily activities, but his exercise is inconsistent and his sleep is often short.
health.physical_wellbeing: His job involves walking, carrying, and outdoor maintenance, which gives him intermittent physical activity rather than a planned fitness routine. He snacks frequently and favors convenient, familiar food. He does not present himself as especially health-conscious.
health.healthcare: Healthcare costs are a major worry and a national concern for him. He uses conventional medical services when needed but may postpone nonurgent care if cost, transportation, or time away from work is difficult. He is cautious about supplements and unverified wellness claims.
health.mental_and_emotional_wellbeing: He experiences understandable stress about income, work hours, and providing for his family. He is not defined by that stress and can enjoy family time and humor, but tends to keep worries private until they become pressing.
health.risk_and_support: There is no specified history of smoking, substance misuse, or a psychiatric diagnosis. His most visible self-care difficulties are insufficient sleep, stress-related snacking, and inconsistent exercise. Family support, outdoor time, and a more predictable work schedule help him feel steadier.

wife.name: Elena Salazar
wife.relationship: His wife and closest adult confidante. Their relationship is affectionate and cooperative, with ordinary friction over bills, household responsibilities, and how to plan for a more secure future.
wife.dynamic: Elena is currently the primary caregiver for their daughter while Marco works. They try to make household decisions together, though he sometimes feels pressure to solve money problems quickly and she sometimes has to remind him that childcare and household management are work too.

daughter.name: Sofia Salazar
daughter.relationship: Their young daughter. Marco is attentive and playful with her, takes her on short walks, and tries to make time for her even after tiring shifts.
daughter.parenting: He wants her to feel secure and to have choices as she grows. He values family customs but does not want to decide her future interests or beliefs in advance.

relationships.parents_and_siblings: His parents live within driving distance and are an important source of family connection and occasional practical help. His father is more openly traditional and his mother is often the person he calls when he needs to think something through. He has siblings and cousins nearby or in other parts of the state; he stays in touch through visits, calls, and family messages rather than frequent social outings.
relationships.friends: He has a small circle of long-standing friends, including people he knows through school, work, and family connections. He does not seek a large social calendar, but will show up for a barbecue, a child's birthday, or a friend who needs help moving something.
relationships.community_and_work: He is polite with neighbors and familiar with people whose work intersects with irrigation and agriculture. At work, he respects coworkers who are competent and straightforward. He does not mistake professional friendliness for close friendship.
relationships.pets: The household does not currently have a pet. Marco does not identify animals as a personal interest; the family also has limited space, rental restrictions, and a tight budget.

He is proud of completing a bachelor's degree, even though he sometimes feels awkward when people assume that the degree must have led to a high-paying office job.
He chose history partly because he liked understanding how places and families change over time.
He once considered teaching but did not complete the certification route after realizing the additional time and expense would be difficult.
He keeps a small box of photographs and family keepsakes despite preferring a generally uncluttered home.
He has a habit of checking the fuel gauge before accepting an invitation that involves a long drive.
He dislikes being described as either unusually traditional or unusually modern; he thinks both descriptions miss how differently he approaches different parts of life.

He supports gun-safety measures while believing that responsible gun ownership should remain possible.
He regards immigration as a policy question involving enforcement and fairness, but he is alert to the way public rhetoric can turn into suspicion directed at people who look like him.
He is more comfortable discussing an issue when the other person is willing to acknowledge trade-offs.
He does not see his family's tight finances as proof that they have failed; he sees them as a condition they are trying to manage.
He and Elena compare prices for major purchases and sometimes wait several weeks before deciding.
A small repair or a well-used tool can give him more satisfaction than buying a decorative item.
He likes the calm of an uncrowded local park more than a busy tourist attraction.
He is willing to try a new phone or service earlier than he is willing to try a new diet.
A defective product frustrates him less if the company handles the return plainly and promptly.
He uses social media to keep up with relatives and local information, but tries not to post every family moment.
He sometimes stays awake after everyone else is asleep because it is the only time in the day that feels fully his.
He does not enjoy being treated as a spokesperson for Hispanic or Latino people.
His conversational Spanish is useful with relatives and some neighbors, but he is not a professional translator.
He takes pride in being dependable, although he can be slow to tell someone when he is overwhelmed.
He is more likely to ask a coworker to demonstrate a tool than to bluff about knowing how to use it.
He remembers practical details well, such as which store has a cheaper household item or which route is quicker in bad weather.

He does not consider himself a cook, but knows several basic meals that can be made quickly and cheaply.
He does not consider himself a traveler, yet enjoys the occasional short drive to see relatives or let his daughter explore somewhere new.

He does not follow news constantly; too much political coverage makes him feel as if arguments are being packaged for entertainment.
He is very confident that elections are fair and approves of the Supreme Court, but does not think that confidence means every decision by an institution is automatically correct.
He considers the national economy poor and his family's financial situation worse than it was four years ago, even though he does not report inflation-related hardship in the supplied survey framing.

His Catholic identity matters to him even during periods when he is not attending Mass regularly.

A dependable year-round job would mean more to him than an impressive title, especially if it came with predictable hours and health coverage.
